approaches.sequence: Coming from the north-west, the hut domes and the landing lanterns show first; the road passes between the huts to the ford. The well roof shows across the water.
approaches.wayfinding: Follow the road through the landing to the ford; the poler's hut stands on the bank above it.

approaches.sequence: Coming down the road from the south-east, the station house roof and its smoke show first, then the well at the junction and the lean-to by the fire; the ford and the huts beyond open up at the junction.
approaches.wayfinding: The road runs past the yard wall to the well junction; the station house path leaves the street there.

causalModel.founding: A mixed village at the road's water point: an Imperial well on the south bench, an Argonian landing on the north bank across the ford. The landing is older than the station.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: Two communities share it because neither can hold the other's half.
causalModel.pressures: The well is Imperial-built and failing. The landing will not help to repair it in stone.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: A perennial spring beside a boat channel, where the road fords the water.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: Would become one community or two villages within a generation.

combatSpaces.why: The street between the well and the ford, where a road fight at the station happens.

districts.notes: The Argonian half on the north strip; no Hist (see siting).

why.microGeography: The dry strip on the ford's north bank, huts on mud pads raised above the high water.
why.playerPurpose: The ford ferry in the wet season and the landing's side of LF83.
why.what: The landing hamlet: three mud huts round an open common, the fish racks and the boats pulled up on the bank.
why.whyHere: The landing is older than the station; its polers came up from the mud-hut country and built as they do at home, on the dry point by the channel.
why.whyNeighbours: It faces the well-station across the ford. It keeps no Hist: its people's tree stands at Fenmarch Village (place.imperial-fringe.fenmarch-village, 1.7 km). They go home for the hatching.

districts.notes: The Imperial half on the south bench.

why.microGeography: A narrow bench between the channel and the hillside, raised on stone pads.
why.playerPurpose: A bed, food for the road, a stable for a horse and water from the well.
why.what: The well-station: the station house, the stable, the lean-to and the well.
why.whyHere: The Imperial half keeps the well and the road trade.
why.whyNeighbours: It faces the landing across the ford, along the road.

networkTerminals.why: The road leaves the ford's north bank toward Blackwood through the landing.
The Blackwood Road arrives from Gideon along the bench to the south-east.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its entrance turns south-east to the common.

why.whyHere: The landing's families live on the dry point by the channel.
why.whyNeighbours: It faces the common with the poler's hut across the road and the store hut to the west.
why.whySpot: West of the road on the north strip, on the widest dry cell.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: type recipe road-station-village (a keeper and travellers); record occupants D1 family (few), D2 travellers (few); roster npcs.json well-keeper and poler
scaleGrounding.why: Two named keepers and one landing family live here; travellers come and go. Six buildings stand, three in the well-station and three in the landing; the dry ground holds no seventh. Beside them stand the well, the lean-to, the ferry raft and the dry-stone walls that hold the two station pads.
